newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New television law for EU screens.
newsitem.headline: New television law for EU screens.

text.p: A new European Union broadcasting law has passed its final hurdle after being adopted by EU ministers, the European Commission said Monday.

The new television without frontiers directive, which was more than two years in the making and involved heated talks among the 15-nation bloc's different institutional actors, was nodded through by EU environment ministers on Friday, it said.
The new law, which EU countries will now have 18 months to apply, leaves unchallenged Hollywood's dominance of the region's television screens.
As under the existing 1989 version of the law, television stations will continue to have to devote more than one half of their screen time to European productions, but only "where practicable."

The legislation innovates in that it guarantees EU viewers for the first time the right to watch major sporting events for free, even if exclusive rights have been bought by pay television channels, provided they appear on a member country's list of protected events.
While stopping short of regulating new internet services, the law provides uniform rules for advertising, TV shopping, protection of minors and sponsorship.

EU Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja, who drew up the plan, said that in the area of digital technology, the law provides a secure legal framework for broadcasters to do their activities through a one-stop-shop, under which broadcasters will only have to comply with the rules in the country in which they are established.
Many members of the European Parliament had fought for a more radically revised directive, with tougher limits on imports from the United States and new rules for new media services.
